conventions.convention: The main regime is nondegenerate level one, charge zero, Λ₀, with finite quantum characteristic e≥2 and ξ≠1. The branches are characteristic zero or characteristic p>0 with p∤e. The numerical Hecke parameter ξ and formal grading variable q are independent.

S(μ) is the left Murphy cell module; right cellular modules convert through star. Its ungraded ordinary comparisons are the same-shape star-contragredient dual and the θ-twisted conjugate Specht module. The twist θ(Tᵣ)=(ξ−1)−Tᵣ reflects residue content.

Tableau order is strong Bruhat order on w_T. For row-strict tableaux, S≤T means every prefix shape of S dominates the corresponding prefix shape of T. Weak edges require both tableaux standard and the smaller consecutive entry in the earlier row-reading node.
Internal shifts satisfy (M{r})ₙ=Mₙ₋ᵣ and q[M]=[M{1}]. Projective K₀ uses split relations; module G₀ uses short exact sequences. Tower groups are restricted direct sums over root contents.
The Hom pairing is first-bar sesquilinear: h(qʳP,qˢM)=qˢ⁻ʳh(P,M). The canonical restricted-dual identification instead uses the bilinear tensor pairing T, with h(P,M)=T(P#,M).

The Hecke diagram anti-involution is defined by transport from KLR; it is not identified with raw Murphy star. Simple normalization uses finite vector duality, while projective normalization uses Hom duality #.

Std_μ is the standard-coordinate functional represented by the orthogonal projection π(M_μ) into the basic module. Restricted Std_λ form a basis of the upper integral dual lattice; raw ambient standard vectors and the lower integral lattice are distinct objects.

Removable nodes are ordered bottom to top in the restriction filtration. Degree counts addable minus removable nodes strictly below the removed node; codegree counts strictly above it in the smaller diagram.

The generic tower helpers use characteristic-zero fields and integer colors, with infinite-order ξ on the nondegenerate side. They do not instantiate the finite cyclic e regime. Their crossings use ψ=−τ, with coefficient series multiplied on the right.

a_{λ,ν}(q) is the multiplicity of normalized positive-characteristic D(λ) in the reduction J(ν) of the characteristic-zero simple. With simple labels as rows and Specht shapes as columns, the factorization is a·d.
AC is inherited through the specified highest-weight, crystal and global-basis suppliers; finite algebra transport introduces no additional choice.

load_bearing.statement: In the specified graded Specht construction, the standard vectors v_T form a homogeneous basis with degree deg(T); the grading is independent of selected reduced decompositions, the KLR generators act in their prescribed degrees, and the character is the sum of q^{deg T}i_T over standard tableaux.

Under inherited AC and the fixed nondegenerate level-one regime, the blockwise graded Hecke–KLR isomorphisms transport the projective highest-weight identification, canonical module restricted-dual identification, normalized functors and pairings in both branches; the lower-projective and upper-simple global-basis identifications additionally hold in characteristic zero under the stated geometric-parameter hypotheses.
In both branches of the nondegenerate level-one regime, for every partition μ, Ψ_can^Hecke([S(μ)])=π(M_μ). Choice is inherited only through the suppliers.

In both branches, restricted Specht modules have irreducible self-dual graded heads; their shifts classify graded simples, with dominance-triangular composition expansions and diagonal multiplicity one. In characteristic zero the intrinsic head equals the normalized simple of the same crystal label. The ordinary signed-conjugate dictionary holds after forgetting grading.

In the specified symmetric Fock model, Std_μ=π(M_μ)=Σ_λ d_{(λ,μ)}(q)G*(λ), summed over restricted labels at the fixed content. Restricted Std_λ form an A-basis of the upper dual lattice; π need not preserve the lower integral lattice.

For a characteristic-zero block in the specified regime, the integer subring generated by the named KLR generator images is a free graded lattice. Its generator-matching base changes to the characteristic-zero field and every stated positive-characteristic field with the same e are graded algebra isomorphisms.

For the specified level-one integer KLR presentation and left graded Murphy cell over any characteristic-zero field in the regime, there is a rational graded cyclic module whose scalar extension preserves the specified initial generator. Rational Garnir kernel lines present it; a nonzero absolutely simple normalized head consequently has a rational initial-generator line and an integral orbit lattice of the asserted rank.

For a nonzero finite-dimensional standard homogeneous cyclotomic KLR module over any field, a successively maximal last-color word detects exactly one normalized simple orbit, with its canonical right crystal label; its word dimension is the product of nil-Hecke factorials. Graded word characters are injective on G₀, and equal characters across fields give equal detected labels.

For characteristic-zero and positive-characteristic fields in the stated regime with the same e, the integer orbit of the specified Specht-generator image is a graded lattice in the normalized simple. Its reduction has the same graded word character, a lattice-independent G₀ class, and canonical restricted-dual image equal to the characteristic-zero upper basis vector.

In the positive-characteristic nondegenerate level-one regime, each normalized cellular head equals the normalized simple of the same right crystal label with shift zero. J(λ) contains that simple once, has only cellular labels dominated by λ, and has a diagram-duality-invariant G₀ class.

seams_checked.note: The consumer retains linear conjugation with reflected colors, restricted basic labels, dominance direction and the distinction between ambient coordinates and the upper integral dual. The supplier does not assert Hecke decomposition-number specialization.

Finite-e BK statements are used in their stated field and parameter regimes. Integer-color generic helpers prove separate local, support and tower results. Fixed normalizing series and transported grading are retained; no universal nontriviality of block gradings is inferred.

Node formulas are transported through J with reflected colors. Ambient all-partition Fock space remains distinct from its basic component; upper coordinates use the restricted Gram inverse. The e=2 double edge and inherited AC are preserved.

Canonical versus KK module normalization, restricted weight duality, first-strand quotient, right append, and the two pairings and dualities are distinguished. The consumer explicitly checks the characteristic-zero geometric-parameter hypotheses before invoking global-basis results.

Same-shape star duality and signed-conjugate comparison retain their separate positions. The explicit unit form factor preserves radicals; right-to-left conversion and residue reflection are stated. Raw Murphy star is not equated with transported diagram duality.

The consumer uses the native crossing sign, PBW and divided-power conventions, maximal-tail reconstruction, absolute simplicity and one-step head/socle statements faithfully. Extremal word dimensions retain nil-Hecke factorial factors rather than being asserted one-dimensional.

The generic degenerate helper uses the same affine generator presentation. Its extension from the supplier's complex-field presentation to arbitrary characteristic-zero fields is proved locally by faithful polynomial operators and PBW reductions; no broader Schur–Weyl conclusion is imported.
